newsitem.title: GERMANY: Police make detentions in German kidnap probe.
newsitem.headline: Police make detentions in German kidnap probe.

text.p: Police searching for kidnapped multi-millionaire Jakub Fiszmann raided buildings and apartments in the Frankfurt area on Wednesday and detained several people.
Prosecutors gave no further details but Fiszmann, 40, was still missing six days after his family paid a four million mark ($2.6 million) ransom.
Police said on Tuesday they believed he was still alive. His only direct contact has been a phone call on October 2, the day after his abduction, saying he that he was kept in a cellar.
His kidnappers, who police think are German criminals, later sent word that he had provisions to survive for four weeks.

Police with helicopters and tracker dogs have been combing the countryside around Frankfurt, including a former U.S. army arms depot. Wednesday's searches were in Frankfurt, Wiesbaden and Mainz, a spokesman for the prosecutors said.

Fiszmann, a member of one of Germany's richest families, runs a property and electronics company in Frankfurt and is also known locally for financing the production of the musical "Tommy" in nearby Offenbach.
He was abducted outside his Frankfurt office on October 1 and his brother Georg paid a four million mark ransom on October 10 to kidnappers who promised to free him the next day.
The Fiszmann family has offered a one millon mark reward for information.
Police believe that his abductors may belong to a gang who tried to extort money during an aborted kidnap of Fiszmann's nephew in 1991.
